idea.Name: pose_confounding_spectral_geometry
idea.Title: Pose-Confounding Spectral Geometry for Full-Wave Inverse-Scattering SLAM
idea.Short Hypothesis: After noise whitening and realification, eliminating unknown pose from the local full-wave inverse-scattering SLAM model produces an effective map-information operator whose finite-dimensional loss is low rank, whose no-prior normalized spectrum is governed by principal angles between map- and pose-induced data tangent spaces, and whose useful information can be improved by genuinely diverse frequencies and trajectories while remaining sensitive to rank events and execution error.
idea.Related Work: The individual ingredients are mature and must not be claimed as novel: Chen-style subspace optimization decomposes induced-current recovery through the current-to-data operator G_S; equivalent Fisher information uses Schur complements to eliminate nuisance parameters; principal angles and finite-rank Hermitian perturbation describe subspace overlap and interlacing; gauge analysis treats identifiability up to group actions; active sensing optimizes Fisher-information criteria. The research question is whether their explicit synthesis for a full-wave volumetric contrast field jointly estimated with platform pose yields a useful, correctly scoped theory and reproducible numerical consequences. Closest overlap must be checked against full-wave inverse-scattering degrees-of-freedom work, inverse scattering with unknown sensor geometry, coherent RF/radar SLAM, RF-SLAM PCRB/identifiability, blind calibration/bilinear inverse problems, and robust experimental design. Novelty is retrieval-bounded; never claim first or no prior work.
idea.Abstract: We study local observability of a volumetric material-contrast map when the transmitting and receiving platform pose is unknown. Starting from a two-dimensional scalar Helmholtz contrast-source model, we derive whitened and realified map and pose Jacobians A and B, and compare the known-pose information K_IS=A^T A with the pose-eliminated information K_SLAM=A^T P_{Range(B)^perp} A and its finite-prior Schur complement K_eff. The finite-dimensional theory links exact map-pose ambiguity to Range(A) intersect Range(B), identifies the no-prior generalized retention spectrum with squared sines of principal angles, and bounds information loss by pose dimension. We then test the theory in a unified CPU-only simulator through analytic-Jacobian checks, rank and spectral identities, gauge and Born-empty-background controls, multi-frequency and equal-budget trajectory comparisons, and first-order robust-sensitivity tests. The study is designed to retain counterexamples: numerical evidence may validate the algebraic implementation, refine conditions, or falsify proposed physical generalizations, but it cannot establish continuum transfer, global nonlinear convergence, online SLAM performance, or global novelty.

datasets: Deterministic synthetic 2D scalar Helmholtz contrast-source scenes on D=[-0.5,0.5]^2, using two smooth nonzero dielectric blobs; begin with small pilot grids and run the specified 32x32 reference plus a 40x40 sensitivity case when CPU cost permits.
One transmitter and 4-8 body-fixed receivers per SE(2) pose, with straight, 90-degree arc, 180-degree arc, and 360-degree circular trajectories matched for path length and measurement count.

Controlled Born/full-wave, single/genuinely-multifrequency/duplicate-block, identity/colored-noise, smooth-basis/pixel-basis, free-pose/finite-prior, anchored/unanchored, and trajectory-perturbation variants with deterministic seeds.
baselines: Known-pose information K_IS versus free-pose K_SLAM and finite-prior K_eff.
Analytic A and B versus centered finite differences of the same forward solver.
Principal-angle closed forms versus generalized eigenvalues on the observable support.
Genuinely distinct frequency blocks versus an exact scaled duplicate block, with no prior, fixed finite prior, and proportionally scaled prior controls.
Full trajectory derivative including pose-Hessian terms versus finite differences and the explicitly labeled frozen-nuisance-subspace approximation.

Sampled worst-case perturbations and the analytic Euclidean-ball gradient direction versus the first-order surrogate; use a Lipschitz lower bound as certified only if a uniform operator-Lipschitz constant over the full ball is derived, otherwise label it empirical.
metrics: Centered finite-difference relative errors and observed O(h^2) region for map and pose Jacobians; state-equation residual and sigma_min(M)/norm(M).
Backward-error-scaled residuals for kernel/rank identity, PSD ordering, loss-rank bound, interlacing, and generalized-spectrum/principal-angle equality; machine-precision rank tolerance only.
Retention eigenvalues rho, principal angles, exact destroyed degrees of freedom, affected-mode count, continuous confusion dimension, log-volume retention, and absolute eigenvalues of K_IS and K_eff.
SE(2) generator cancellation residuals, Born empty-background bilinear scaling, and anchor/symmetry controls.
Frequency-stacking PSD increments, shared-compensation residuals, duplicate-block invariance controls, and equal-budget trajectory comparisons.

First-order eigenvalue prediction error versus perturbation radius, spectral gaps, sigma_min(B), projector movement, sampled/analytic worst case, explicitly certified-or-empirical Lipschitz lower-bound checks, and frozen-nuisance approximation error.
Exact commands, configs, random seeds, runtime/environment record, result tables, figure paths, and SHA-256 hashes.
Experiments.compute_estimate: Apple Silicon CPU only. Use staged resolution: cheap algebraic/Jacobian falsifiers first, then the 32x32 reference sweeps and a limited 40x40 discretization check. Reuse Green matrices and factorizations. No CUDA, GPU Docker, neural-network training, daemon, scheduler, database, web UI, or new orchestration framework. Report actual runtime and any family that cannot be completed rather than silently reducing scope.
steps: Before coding, read /Volumes/migodam's-external-brain/Research/Inv_SLAM/research/agentic_input/workshop.md and the three source files it names. Preserve its status ledger and semantic-drift prohibitions.

Family 1: implement the 2D forward solver and analytic A/B builders; verify centered map/pose derivatives across h, solver residuals, weak-scattering Born/full-wave asymptotics, and non-resonant conditioning.

Family 2: after whitening and realification, verify kernel/rank identities, rho=sin^2(theta), loss-rank and interlacing, prior ordering and limits, and distinguish generalized retention directions from ordinary K_IS eigenmodes.
Family 3: construct smooth-basis SE(2) gauge generators with anchor/symmetry controls; separately verify B=0 at Born empty background and the leading bilinear sensing-operator mismatch.

Family 4: compare genuinely diverse and exactly duplicate frequencies using one shared pose compensation; test absolute-information monotonicity and the correctly qualified duplicate-block result; compare four equal-budget trajectories without assuming their ordering is universal.

Family 5: verify full trajectory/eigenvalue derivatives in positive-gap regions, test the robust first-order surrogate using both the analytic adverse direction and random boundary samples, quantify frozen-nuisance error, and deliberately expose near-crossing/rank-event breakdown.

For every family write a hypothesis/claim-status table, exact executed checks, metrics, pass/fail interpretation, artifacts, and a cannot-establish section. A counterexample or corrected condition is an acceptable result.

Synthesize only results supported by executed artifacts. Keep finite-dimensional proofs, conditional full-wave derivations, numerical observations, and open continuum/transversality/rank-event conjectures visibly separate.
Prepare a full English LaTeX/PDF manuscript draft with AI-use disclosure, verified citations, reproducibility appendix, limitations, and explicit negative results.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The local tangent/Fisher theory does not address cycle skipping, phase wrapping, wrong data association, posterior multimodality, or basin of attraction; practical claims must be scoped accordingly.
Complex measurements with real physical parameters require whitening followed by realification; using a complex pose projector would enlarge the nuisance space and invalidate the interpretation.
Current-space G_S/SOM modes are not map-Jacobian or K_eff modes; any conflation is a fatal semantic error.

SOM may be presented as a current-space computational substrate, but not as the same subspace as the pose-confounding map-tangent spectrum unless an explicit A=G_S T_chi pullback/composition result is proved and implemented.
Exact SE(2) gauge requires a symmetry-compatible background/domain; bounded grids, anchors, known background, and scene symmetry can break or degenerate generators.
At Born empty background, first-order B vanishes; pose effects then form a bilinear operator-uncertainty problem and cannot be declared harmless.

Finite-prior retention is weighted shrinkage, not ordinary squared-sine principal angles. Duplicate-block rho invariance holds only with no prior or matching prior scaling, not with a fixed finite prior.
Finite-dimensional numerical identities do not prove stable transversality or closed-range properties of the continuum inverse problem; discretization refinement is diagnostic only.
Trajectory derivative claims require smoothness, locally constant rank, and spectral gaps; rank events and repeated eigenvalues need cluster/projector treatment.
The independent ScholarQA evidence bundle is partial because of Semantic Scholar rate limits. Final citations must be verified and novelty claims bounded to retrieved records.
All five experiment families are required attempts, but CPU limits may force an explicitly documented partial result; passing them is bounded model evidence, not production or real-world acceptance.

report.summary: The round continued the existing pose-confounded spectral-geometry study in the same working directory and added six new empirical families/controls plus a consolidated synthesis and updated manuscript. The algebraic spine holds under colored noise and across finite-grid refinement; the current-space G_S/SOM subspace is verified to be distinct from the map-tangent A/K_eff subspace; replications are mostly stable with one preserved machine-rank boundary event; and a much tighter operator-Lipschitz bound is reported for the affine tangent layer, with the full nonlinear bound explicitly left non-certified. A previously proposed trajectory ordering hypothesis remains false under both raw and normalized controls.
key_results: Family 6 colored noise: analytic whitening residual ||W C W^H - I||/||I|| ~ 7e-16; rank identity residual 0; retention principal-angle identity max diff 1.8e-15; no-prior duplicate-block invariance holds while fixed prior breaks it.
Family 6 SNR sweep: frequency-diversity movement is non-monotone in the second frequency's SNR, peaking near balanced SNR (0.128/0.235/0.569) and reaching a finite positive high-SNR plateau.

Family 4c same-standoff/per-pose-energy normalization: normalization verified to 2.2e-16; raw and normalized trajectory orderings do not flip; trajectory-order claim remains a preserved counterexample: arc90 > straight > arc180 > circle360, with arc270 lowest.

Family 7 refinement/rank: N=16/24/32/40/48 ranks constant (rA=24, rB=18, rAB=42); theta_min decreases monotonically 4.253e-4 to 4.188e-4 deg; near-confounded count constant at 4; zero rank events over f in [0.6,2.6]; Born/empty-background gates pass; Born-vs-full discrepancy grows to 0.197 at s=1.

Family 8 SOM/map-tangent distinction: full-wave composition A = G_S M^{-1} diag(E_tot) verified bit-identical; Range(A) is contained in Range(G_S) machine-exactly, but right singular subspaces are strongly distinct (median principal angle 29.7 deg, 0/24 below 1e-8 deg); K_eff confounded directions are nearly orthogonal to both mode families (overlaps ~3e-3 vs ~6e-8).

Family 9 replications/ablation: over 7 scenes retention identity 7/7, frequency diversity 7/7, rank identity 6/7 with one ring-scene machine-rank boundary event preserved; pose-DOF ablation retained DOF: known-pose 24.0, x-only 18.0, y-only 18.0, theta-only 21.4, xy 12.6, full 9.4.

Families 5b/5b2 operator-Lipschitz: alpha-aware bound L_struct = 1.124e-2, about 1.25e9 times tighter than the loose bound 1.408e7; affine tangent certificate has zero violations up to epsilon=0.1 over 2000 directions; full nonlinear model has no sampled violations but is honestly labeled a derived structural bound with sampled envelope, not a formal interval certificate.
Writeup consolidation: manuscript/main_round2.tex and manuscript/main_round2.pdf produced, 34 pages, 2.1 MB, no unresolved references, 14 figure paths verified.
completed_steps: Implemented and ran Family 6 colored-noise/per-frequency SNR whitening with Matern-1/2 receiver correlation and consistent complex Jacobian whitening/realification.
Implemented and ran Family 4c same-standoff/per-pose-energy-normalized trajectory control and compared raw vs normalized orderings.
Implemented and ran Family 7 resolution, rank-event, and stable-transversality diagnostics across N=16/24/32/40/48.
Implemented and ran Family 8 G_S/SOM vs map-tangent A/K_eff distinction checks, including composition identities and subspace angle comparisons.
Implemented and ran Family 9 seed replications and pose-DOF/receiver/pose-count/basis ablations.
Ran precursor Family 5b loose Lipschitz bound and corrected Family 5b2 alpha-aware tight bound, with affine tangent and sampled nonlinear checks.
Consolidated all new artifacts into notes/synthesis_round2.md and updated manuscript/main_round2.tex/pdf.
dead_ends: The Family-4 trajectory-order hypothesis remains false under both raw and normalized controls; this is recorded as a preserved counterexample, not a universal claim.
Formal interval certification of the full nonlinear Helmholtz operator-Lipschitz constant is still open; only the affine tangent certificate is rigorous and conditional on FD-accurate Jacobians.
Family 7 resolution diagnostics are finite-grid only; literal near-crossing flags are numerical-null artifacts, not certified continuum crossings or rank events.
Fixed finite prior breaks duplicate-block no-prior invariance in the colored-noise family, confirming a known scoping condition.
Family 9 rank identity is 6/7, with one ring-scene machine-rank boundary event preserved rather than resolved into a universal rank result.
Family 6 receiver-correlation sweep was recorded as an observation without a forced pass/fail claim.
next_steps: Attempt a true interval-arithmetic certificate of the full nonlinear operator-Lipschitz constant by bounding pose-dependent Green-function ingredients, or import a rigorous Hankel/interval bound.
Scale to a pilot 3D scalar or vector Helmholtz extension while keeping the G_S/current-space vs map-tangent A/K_eff distinction explicit.

Run a small nonlinear least-squares/online SLAM toy to test whether the retained/confounded spectral predictions track actual joint map+pose posterior uncertainty, kept strictly separate from the finite-dimensional theory.
Formalize and possibly replicate the non-monotonic SNR-dependent frequency-diversity curve, especially the finite high-SNR plateau.
If needed, verify the 34-page manuscript figures and citations against the final result JSONs and notes before submission.

unresolved_issues: Trajectory design result is still a single-setting counterexample: the arc90 > straight > arc180 > circle360 ordering was preserved in one controlled comparison, but it has not been replicated across multiple scenes, frequencies, or trajectory parameter variations. A full paper needs either a robust replicated negative/design result or a mechanistic explanation for when and why a trajectory helps.

Frequency-diversity support is too narrow: the SNR sweep shows non-monotonic behavior for the second frequency, but only a two-frequency setup is reported. Broader frequency-set/bandwidth sweeps and multiple scenes are needed to support any claim about when genuinely diverse frequencies improve pose-eliminated information.

The full nonlinear operator-Lipschitz bound remains non-certified. The affine tangent certificate is strong, but the manuscript must either formally certify the nonlinear bound or explicitly demote all execution-error robustness claims to empirical/structural observations; sampled zero violations are not sufficient for a top-venue robustness result.

One machine-rank boundary event appeared in the Family 9 replications, so the central rank/kernel identity is not uniformly clean across the seven scenes. This event needs to be investigated with stable-rank/truncated-SVD diagnostics, tolerance sweeps, and scene-conditioning controls before the algebraic spine can be considered fully locked.

The study lacks any external comparison or literature-derived quantitative check beyond internal algebraic controls. At least one comparison with an existing inverse-scattering/PCRB or RF-SLAM information bound would strengthen the paper's positioning and show the results are not only self-consistent.

All empirical evidence is from a single 2D scalar Helmholtz model. If feasible, a second model/geometry or more severe discretization/conditioning variation should be added, or the manuscript should more sharply scope the claims as strictly model-specific finite-dimensional verification.
verdict.reasoning: This is a substantial and carefully executed study, not a thin pilot. The whitening/realification algebraic spine is verified to machine precision, the principal-angle retention identity holds under colored noise and grid refinement, the SOM/map-tangent distinction is clearly established, and the affine tangent Lipschitz certificate is meaningful. The preserved negative trajectory ordering and non-monotone SNR diversity are honest and potentially valuable. However, the full-paper bar is not yet met for the design and robustness parts of the hypothesis. The trajectory counterexample is still single-setting and not replicated across scenes or frequencies; frequency diversity is tested too narrowly; the nonlinear robustness claim is explicitly non-certified; one rank-boundary replication event remains unresolved; and there is no external comparison. These are not reasons to abandon the idea, but they require a focused deepening and reframing before the manuscript is ready as a full-length paper.
